dialogue.text: Dr. Schäf. It sounds good, no? Your flight leaves from the end of the runway.
Balzac will miss you. He won't say it. He is a dog.
Macau is far, but a good proof works in every time zone.
Two papers on doomed code. I think that is a thesis. Let's do the defense. Right now.
Question one: what is a doomed program point?

choices.text: A statement that fails on every execution that reaches it.
Any line that Reviewer #2 doesn't like.

dialogue.text: Balzac growls. Think about it and come back.
Good. Question two: how do you show a point is doomed?

choices.text: Prove that no execution through it can terminate normally.
Run the program once and see if it crashes.

dialogue.text: That is testing, not proving. Balzac is disappointed. Come back when you're ready.
Stephan is busy clicking buttons. Balzac is disappointed. Come back when you're ready.
Last question. Balzac will ask it.
Woof?
Balzac accepts. Congratulations, Dr. Schäf!
How is the research going? So far I count {papersHere}. A thesis needs at least two papers.
Your papers are somewhere out there. The forest path, the wine hill, the city. Balzac found one near the Münster once.
Martin! Welcome to Freiburg. Your office is here, at the old Flugplatz. Planes used to land here. Now only ideas.
This is Balzac. He is in the group. He does not publish, but he reviews.
Your first task: find code that is doomed. Code that can only fail. Nobody can prove it's there, so we will.
Write two papers about it and come back. Then we talk about your defense.
Martin! Fellow PhD student, Stephan. Office across the hall. I'm working on GUI testing. Please don't tell anyone that's a real field.
I clicked every button in this application 4,000 times. Then I wrote a program to click them for me. That's the whole thesis.
If you ever go somewhere far away for a postdoc, tell me. I'm coming too. Someone has to test your GUIs.
Balzac sat on my keyboard again. The paper improved.
The Mercedes made it all the way from Saarbrücken. The heater is still stuck. It's a feature now.
High school, university, and now a PhD in the same group. At this point I'm following you, or you're following me.
Brunch in Boetzingen on Sunday? The wine hill is right there. We'll just look at it.
I've been thinking: when a program fails, which parts of the trace actually matter? One day I'll turn that into a paper.
(A visitor is scribbling termination proofs with Andreas. He nods at you and keeps writing.)
Hm? Oh, hi. Sorry, busy. We're proving this loop terminates. It's been three days.
(He waves vaguely. You won't really talk until New York, many years from now.)
